tasks.title: Aggregate multiple input files
tasks.prompt:
Add repeatable --input PATH arguments after the existing positional input.
Read the positional file first, then each additional file in argument order,
and produce one aggregate report. Do not deduplicate paths: passing a file
twice intentionally counts its events twice. Keep the existing --top option,
JSON schema, UTF-8 support, and deterministic ordering. Validate every file
before replacing the output. An unreadable or malformed later file is a user
error; identify the file and, for malformed JSONL, its physical line number.
Preserve any prior output report on failure.

tasks.title: Select services and a severity threshold
tasks.prompt:
Add repeatable --service NAME filters and optional --min-severity LEVEL.
Repeated services form a union; no service filter means all services.
Severity order is info < warning < error and the default threshold is info.
When both options are present, an event must satisfy both filters. Compute the
existing report over selected events only. Preserve zero entries in
by_severity. Parse and validate every input event even when it would be filtered
out, so invalid input is never silently accepted. Unknown severity arguments
are user errors and cannot replace an existing output.

tasks.title: Export a service-by-severity CSV summary
tasks.prompt:
Add --format csv as an alternative to the default JSON format. CSV has the
header service,info,warning,error,total and one row for each service in
lexicographic service-name order. Counts include zeros. Use standard CSV
quoting and UTF-8, so service names containing commas, quotes, or newlines
round-trip through Python's csv module. No total/footer row is added. Empty
input produces only the header. JSON output, including --top, is unchanged;
--top does not affect CSV counts. Validate all input before replacing the
output file and preserve the existing error behavior.

tasks.title: Explicit streaming mode to stdout
tasks.prompt:
Add --stream to validate and emit events as JSON Lines on stdout, without
aggregation. In this mode --output must be omitted; combining them is a user
error. Preserve input order and ignore blank lines. Each valid event is emitted
as a JSON object with only service, severity, and message plus a newline.
Process input incrementally: on malformed later input, previously emitted
events remain on stdout, the command returns 2, and stderr identifies the
physical line. Do not buffer all events until end of input, write a temporary
report, or alter normal report-file behavior. Extra input keys are omitted.

tasks.title: Cancel a queued task
tasks.prompt:
Add cancel DB TASK_ID. Only a task whose stored state is queued may be
cancelled. Remove that queued task atomically and print {"cancelled":true}.
Unknown task IDs are an idempotent success with {"cancelled":false}.
Leased, completed, and dead tasks are user errors and must remain unchanged.
Do not expire leases as a side effect of cancel. Preserve all existing queue
commands and use the normal one-line JSON/no-traceback error contract.

tasks.title: Extend a currently owned lease
tasks.prompt:
Add extend DB TASK_ID WORKER LEASE_TOKEN --lease-seconds N [--now SECONDS].
Only the current owner/token of an unexpired leased task may extend it.
N must be positive and finite; --now uses the seed's finite logical-clock
contract. The new expiry is max(current_expiry, now + N), so an extension never
shortens the lease. Return task_id, lease_token, and lease_expires_at in one
JSON object. Do not increment attempts, rotate the token, or change payloads.
Unknown, expired, stale-token, or wrong-owner requests are user errors and
must not alter the database. Preserve existing commands.

tasks.title: Atomically enqueue a JSON batch
tasks.prompt:
Add enqueue-batch DB INPUT.json. The input is an array of objects containing
task_id and payload, with optional priority and max_attempts following enqueue's
existing defaults and validation. Reject unknown object keys and duplicate IDs
within the batch. Validate the entire batch before changing the database.
An existing task with equivalent payload/options is an idempotent match; a
conflict aborts the whole batch. On success print {"created":N,"existing":M}.
An empty batch succeeds with zero counts. All inserted tasks and counts must
be committed atomically; preserve existing single-task behavior.

tasks.title: Read-only inspection of an expired lease
tasks.prompt:
Add inspect DB TASK_ID [--now SECONDS] for diagnostics. This operation is
read-only, including for an expired lease. Print null for an unknown task.
For an existing task print task_id, payload, stored_state, attempts, and
lease_expired. lease_expired is true only when stored_state is leased and its
expiry is at or before the chosen finite time. Do not requeue an expired task,
increment attempts, change tokens, update counters, or create a missing DB.
A missing database or invalid time is a normal user error. Preserve stats'
existing behavior: stats may still materialize expirations.

tasks.title: Execute selected targets and their prerequisites
tasks.prompt:
Add repeatable --target TASK_ID arguments. With no targets, execute the whole
plan as before. Otherwise execute each requested task and its transitive
prerequisites exactly once; duplicate target options are harmless. Validate the
entire original plan before any command starts, including tasks outside the
selected closure. Unknown targets are validation errors. Reports contain the
selected closure only, in original input order, with unchanged task-result
schema and exit-status rules. Do not run unrelated commands.

tasks.title: Per-task environment overrides
tasks.prompt:
Allow optional env on each task: an object mapping environment-variable names
to string values. Valid names are non-empty strings without '=' or NUL; values
must be strings without NUL. Overlay these entries on the runner's inherited
environment for that task only, keeping inherited variables not mentioned.
Validate every env object before starting any command. Do not expand shell
syntax in values, mutate the parent environment, or leak one task's overrides
into another. Preserve structured argv, retries, report schema, and other plan
behavior.

tasks.title: Task-specific successful exit codes
tasks.prompt:
Allow optional success_codes per task, a non-empty array of distinct integers
from 0 through 255. Booleans are not valid integers for this field. The default
remains [0]. A process exit code in this set marks that task successful and
unblocks dependents without retrying it. Other exit codes retain existing
retry/failure behavior. Preserve the actual process exit_code in the report.
Validate all success_codes before launching commands, and preserve current
timeout, signal-termination, ordering, and overall exit-status behavior.

tasks.title: Plan preview without execution or report replacement
tasks.prompt:
Add --dry-run to validate a complete plan and print its deterministic execution
layers on stdout without running subprocesses or replacing --output. Output is
one JSON object {"layers":[[TASK_ID,...],...]} plus newline. Layer zero contains
tasks with no dependencies; each following layer contains tasks whose
dependencies are all in previous layers. Sort IDs within each layer. This is a
dependency preview, not a resource/concurrency schedule, so jobs and resource
labels do not move a task between layers. Invalid plans retain the existing
validation error behavior. Normal execution remains unchanged.
